description: A complete AI agency at your fingertips - From frontend wizards to Reddit community ninjas, from whimsy injectors to reality checkers. Each agent is a specialized expert with personality, processes, and proven deliverables.

summary.one_liner: A large collection of role-specific AI agent personality files (engineering, design, marketing, sales, security, legal, finance and more) that can be installed into tools such as Claude Code, Cursor, Codex and Gemini CLI.
keywords: replace hiring a dev team with ai
summary.what_it_does: The repository is a catalog of AI agent definitions, each written as a markdown file describing a specialist's identity, personality, mission, workflows, deliverables and success metrics. The roster is organized into divisions such as Engineering, Design, Paid Media, Sales, Marketing, Product, Project Management, Testing, Security, Support, Spatial Computing, Specialized, Finance and Game Development, with many tables listing each agent's specialty and when to use it. Shell scripts (scripts/install.sh and scripts/convert.sh) can generate integration files and install selected agents or whole divisions into supported tools, with options to pick teams, list agents, or run a dry run. Users can also copy individual agent files into a tool's agent directory or use them as reference material. The README also mentions a separate native desktop app that browses the roster and installs agents with a click.
use_cases: Installing specialist agent personas into Claude Code or Cursor
Finding a ready-made prompt for a specific role like frontend developer or SRE
Assembling a team of AI agents for a startup or project
Adapting agent prompts as templates for custom assistants
Generating tool-specific agent files for multiple AI coding assistants
Reviewing code, testing, or security using specialized agent prompts
how_to_run: brew install --cask msitarzewski/agency-agents/agency-agents (macOS, desktop app route)
stack: Python (used in a README example for runbook rosters)
notable: Very broad roster of several hundred role-specific agents across dozens of divisions
One install script targets about 15 AI coding tools, with interactive or per-division and per-agent selection
Supports dry-run installs and team/runbook-based rosters such as startup-mvp
Includes many region-specific agents (China platforms, French, Korean, US federal compliance)
Companion native desktop app for browsing and installing agents with auto-update
caveats: OpenCode runtime reportedly registers only about 119 agents and silently drops the rest, so large installs need --division subsets
Agents are prompt personas rather than executable software; output quality depends on the underlying model and tool
The README does not state a license beyond the GitHub metadata; the desktop app is a separate download
